modelNotes: Minutes Engine 1.1 uses player-pool status plus season, last 5, and last 10 minutes from NBA history.
Unknown starters retain their historical minutes baseline and are not treated as confirmed bench players.
Missing injury information does not mean a player is cleared; publication eligibility requires confirmed game status and role.
Roles are Core Starter, Starter, Rotation, Bench, Deep Bench, and Inactive.
No odds or betting lines are used.

injury.shortComment: Miller amassed 28 points (10-19 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, four assists and one block in 32 minutes during Tuesday's 118-114 overtime loss to the Lakers.
injury.detail: Miller bounced back from a miserable shooting night against the Clippers and led Charlotte in scoring, though a costly turnover in the final seconds of regulation helped open the door for the Lakers' rally. Efficiency has been an issue for the forward all season, so this was one of his better shooting performances. With Kon Knueppel (hamstring) sidelined, Miller remains the focal point of the Hornets' offense.

injury.detail: Hunter has been bothered by left hip soreness. While it kept him off the floor for Sunday's 125-103 loss to the Thunder, he returned for Wednesday's meeting with the Suns. If Hunter can't suit up Friday, it could mean more minutes for Leaky Black and Alex Karaban.

injury.shortComment: Murray-Boyles (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Pistons.
injury.detail: Murray-Boyles has been placed in the league's concussion protocol after leaving Wednesday's loss to the Wizards with what was initially called an illness. With the second-year big man sidelined, Jakob Poeltl, Kyle Anderson and Trayce Jackson-Davis are all candidates for increased playing time. Murray-Boyles' next chance to play will come Monday against Milwaukee.

injury.shortComment: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
injury.detail: Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

injury.shortComment: Flemings (back) is out for Friday's game against the Hornets, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injury.detail: Friday will mark Flemings' third straight game on the inactive list, which should result in another start for Aaron Wiggins, and Luguentz Dort will have the chance for some extended minutes. For now, Flemings should be considered questionable for Sunday's meeting with the Pistons.

injury.shortComment: Head coach JJ Redick said he expects Reaves (heel) to return for Monday's matchup with Utah or Friday's game in San Antonio, Mark Medina of TheSportingTribune.com reports.
injury.detail: Reaves will miss his fourth straight game Friday, but it sounds like he'll be back next week. Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton will continue to pick up the slack while Reaves is out, and Luka Doncic will be operating with a hefty usage rate.

injury.shortComment: Capela (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Denver.
injury.detail: Capela hasn't taken the court since suffering a right ankle sprain against the Thunder on Oct. 31. His next opportunity to return will arrive Monday against the Clippers.

injury.shortComment: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury.detail: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Achiuwa (lower leg) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Lakers.
injury.detail: Achiuwa will miss the front end of this back-to-back set due to a lower-leg contusion, and his next chance to play will come against Boston on Saturday. With the 27-year-old sidelined, Dylan Cardwell and Alex Karaban are candidates for increased playing time.

injury.shortComment: Onyenso agreed to a two-way contract with the Pistons on Thursday.
injury.detail: The No. 53 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Onyenso appears poised to see run in the G League after putting pen to paper on a two-way deal. He'll likely face an uphill battle to carve out a role in the rotation, so Detroit will presumably allow him to continue his development with Motor City.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Caruso (hip) is listed as out for Friday's game against the Pelicans.
injury.detail: Caruso exited Wednesday's 117-112 loss to the Hawks because of a hip issue. He will now miss his fourth game of the 2026-27 campaign, with his next opportunity to play coming Sunday in Miami. With Caruso sidelined, it could mean more minutes for Bennett Stirtz and Nique Clifford.

injury.shortComment: Newell underwent surgery Tuesday for a plantar plate tear in his left great toe, and he will be re-evaluated in approximately four months, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injury.detail: Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
injury.detail: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

injury.shortComment: Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
injury.detail: Mathurin will miss a fourth straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the undermanned Pelicans moving forward, while Mathurin can be deemed week-to-week.

injury.shortComment: McGowens (elbow) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
injury.detail: McGowens will miss a fifth consecutive contest due to an infection in his left elbow. He's without a timetable to return and can be considered week-to-week until the Pelicans offer an update on his status.

injury.shortComment: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

injury.shortComment: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
injury.detail: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

injury.shortComment: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
injury.detail: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

injury.shortComment: McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.
injury.detail: The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.

injury.shortComment: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
injury.detail: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

injury.shortComment: Robinson will be re-evaluated in one week due to a left quadriceps strain, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
injury.detail: Robinson has gotten off to a strong start this season, though he's now expected to miss at least the next week after appearing in each of Detroit's first 12 regular-season games. The sharpshooter is averaging 17.4 points in 30.5 minutes per contest, and his absence will open up additional minutes for Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green.

injury.shortComment: Okorie (oblique) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Toronto.
injury.detail: Okorie is dealing with a left oblique strain he sustained while playing for the G League's Motor City Cruise. The rookie first-rounder's next opportunity to play for the parent club will come Sunday at Atlanta.

injury.shortComment: Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days.
injury.detail: Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

injury.shortComment: Okpara (illness) is available for Friday's game against Toronto.
injury.detail: Okpara will shed his questionable tag due to an illness and suit up Friday. However, the two-way player isn't guaranteed to see the floor.

injury.shortComment: Nelson (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Orlando.
injury.detail: Nelson will hit the inactive list due to a sprained right ankle. The two-way player's absence shouldn't affect the rotation.

injury.shortComment: Williams (hamstring) is listed as out for Friday's game versus the Hawks.
injury.detail: Williams started in Tuesday's 118-114 loss to the Lakers, but he will sit out Friday to rest. With Grayson Allen (concussion) also sidelined, Royce O'Neale could find his way into the starting lineup.

injury.shortComment: Allen (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Atlanta.
injury.detail: Allen is currently dealing with concussion-like symptoms and is in line for a second straight absence. Sion James and Royce O'Neale should continue to see an uptick in playing time until Allen is cleared to return.

injury.shortComment: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
injury.detail: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Sean Sweeney said Wednesday that Nelson (ankle) has been doing "some on-court stuff," though Sweeney added that the work has been "minimal," Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
injury.detail: Nelson underwent surgery this offseason to repair a fractured left ankle. It's encouraging to hear that he's made some progress, but the two-way player can still be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injury.shortComment: Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
injury.detail: Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.

injury.shortComment: Smith (illness) is out for Friday's game against the Wizards, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
injury.detail: With Smith unavailable after being downgraded to questionable earlier Friday, Chicago will need to cover his center minutes elsewhere. His absence opens up added frontcourt work most prominently for Zach Collins and Nic Claxton, the latter of whom is the likelier candidate to start at center.

injury.shortComment: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
injury.detail: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

injury.shortComment: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
injury.detail: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

injury.shortComment: Tyson (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Indiana.
injury.detail: Tyson will miss a third consecutive contest due to a right ankle injury, and his next chance to play will come Monday at Chicago. With Evan Mobley (toe) out and Peyton Watson (back) questionable, Tyrese Proctor, Meleek Thomas and Mario Hezonja could all see increased playing time once again.

injury.shortComment: Landale (hip) won't play in Friday's game against the Hornets, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injury.detail: The big man's next chance to play comes Sunday against the Pistons. Zuby Ejiofor should remain in the rotation as the No. 2 center until Landale returns.

injury.shortComment: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
injury.detail: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

injury.shortComment: Isaac (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Celtics.
injury.detail: Isaac's 2026-27 season debut will have to wait, as he's still working his way back from a left knee injury. He should be considered week-to-week until Orlando provides a clear update for his return.

injury.shortComment: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
injury.detail: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

injury.shortComment: Leonard (knee) could return in the next few weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury.detail: This was the expectation after the Raptors ruled out the star forward Tuesday for at least one more week. Collin Murray-Boyles should continue to handle a larger role once he passes the concussion protocol, and Ja'Kobe Walter should remain a starter for the time being.

injury.shortComment: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
injury.detail: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

injury.shortComment: Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injury.detail: The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

injury.shortComment: Tomlin (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
injury.detail: Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

injury.shortComment: Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet.ca reports.
injury.detail: Bittle is still working his way back from a foot fracture that has plagued him for multiple months, and he remains without a clear return timeline. He can be considered week-to-week for the time being.

injury.shortComment: Topic (hip) is out for Friday's game against New Orleans.
injury.detail: Topic suffered a hip injury during Wednesday's matchup against Atlanta, and the issue is significant enough to keep him from Friday's game. His next opportunity to return will arrive Sunday in Miami.

injury.shortComment: Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
injury.detail: Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

injury.shortComment: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

injury.shortComment: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
injury.detail: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

injury.shortComment: Barrett has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injury.detail: Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

injury.shortComment: Holland (knee) is listed as out for Friday's game against Toronto.
injury.detail: Holland was listed as doubtful, so most expected he would miss his third consecutive game. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday in Atlanta. In the meantime, Chaz Lanier and Isaiah Joe should continue to see more minutes.

injury.shortComment: Prince (knee) underwent surgery to address lingering issues and has no timeline for a return, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
injury.detail: With Detroit still without a return timetable for Prince after right knee surgery, he appears set for an extended absence well beyond Friday's tilt against Toronto. Prince hasn't been a significant part of the Pistons' rotation this season, so his continued absence is unlikely to create a major fantasy ripple effect.

injury.shortComment: Sorber underwent an arthroscopic knee procedure Tuesday to address inflammation at the patellofemoral joint in his right knee, and he's expected to return to on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, Steve McGehee of News 9 Oklahoma City reports.
injury.detail: Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

injury.shortComment: Awaka (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
injury.detail: Awaka is missing a fifth straight contest due to a back problem. The rookie big man can be considered week-to-week going forward.

injury.shortComment: Watford (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Oklahoma City.
injury.detail: Watford will miss a seventh consecutive contest due to a right ankle sprain. He remains without a definitive return timetable.

injury.shortComment: Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Memphis.
injury.detail: Vukcevic has yet to make his season debut due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards offer an update on his progress.

injury.shortComment: Haliburton (hamstring) is expected to miss at least two more weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Haliburton hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a left hamstring strain, and the Pacers won't rush him back. With the star floor general unlikely to return until mid-December at the earliest, Quenton Jackson and T.J. McConnell are candidates for increased playing time, while Andrew Nembhard figures to continue seeing increased playmaking duties.

injury.shortComment: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
injury.detail: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

injury.shortComment: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
injury.detail: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

injury.shortComment: Nurkic (foot) has been cleared for on-court work and will be re-evaluated in one week.
injury.detail: Nurkic continues to make progress in his recovery from a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe on his right foot, and getting cleared for on-court work is a big step in his rehab. There are still a few steps he'll need to clear before he makes his return to the floor, but once he's able to get through full-contact, 5-on-5 work, we'll know he's close.

injury.shortComment: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

injury.shortComment: Raynaud (knee) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
injury.detail: Raynaud continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff, suggesting he's still not close. He should be considered week-to-week moving forward.
